Electronic Components

 SMD Resistor Code: How to Read 3 Digit, 4 Digit and EIA 96 Markings, R Notation, 0 Ohm Jumpers and Package Power Ratings

 Those tiny black chips on every PCB carry their value as a short printed code. Learn to decode all three marking systems, check the power rating of the package and test a doubtful part with confidence.

 
 3 and 4 Digit Codes 
 EIA 96 Chart 
 R Notation 
 Package Sizes 
 Calculator 
 




 An SMD resistor code is a short marking that tells you the resistance of a chip resistor without a meter. This guide covers every common system, a full EIA 96 table, package power ratings and a decoder calculator.


 
 Hello everyone, today we are going to learn how to read any smd resistor code, from simple 3 digit markings to EIA 96 letters, along with the power each package can handle.


 
 
 
 What Is an SMD Resistor Code?

 An smd resistor code is the number or letter marking printed on a surface mount chip resistor that gives its resistance value in a compact form. The three common systems are the 3 digit code, the 4 digit code and the EIA 96 code, with the letter R used as a decimal point.

 
 
 Marking System Value 

 472 3 digit 47 × 10² = 4.7 kΩ 

 103 3 digit 10 × 10³ = 10 kΩ 

 4702 4 digit 470 × 10² = 47 kΩ 

 4R7 R notation 4.7 Ω 

 01C EIA 96 100 × 100 = 10 kΩ 

 000 Jumper 0 Ω link 

 


 The last digit of a numeric smd resistor code is always the multiplier, written as the number of zeros to add after the significant digits. Once you remember that one rule, most of the codes on an industrial PCB can be read in seconds.

 
 
 Image credit: JLCPCB . Chart courtesy of JLCPCB, shown here for educational reference. 
 
 Through hole parts use colour bands instead, as explained in our resistor color code guide . Chip parts are too small for bands, so a printed number is the cheaper option for the manufacturer.

 Do You Know?
 JLCPCB notes that most 0201 and 01005 resistors carry no marking at all because the body is too small to print on. For these parts the bill of materials and the pick and place file are the only reliable record.



 
 
 Advertisement 


 
 


 How to Read an SMD Resistor Code With 3 Digits

 The 3 digit system is used for 2 %, 5 % and 10 % tolerance parts in the E24 series, according to the Vishay marking document. The first two digits are the significant figures and the third digit is the power of ten.

 
Value = first two digits × 10^(third digit)
472 = 47 × 10² = 4700 Ω
 472 = 4.7 kΩ 
220 = 22 × 10⁰ = 22 Ω


 A third digit of 0 means no zeros, so 100 is 10 Ω and not 100 Ω, which is the most common reading error by beginners. Values under 10 Ω cannot use this format, so the letter R takes over, as shown in the next section.

 
 
 3 digit smd resistor code Value Common use 

 100 10 Ω Gate and series resistors 

 221 220 Ω LED current limit 

 102 1 kΩ Base resistors 

 472 4.7 kΩ I2C pull up 

 103 10 kΩ Pull up and pull down
